game: NYJ@NE Week 6 2026, NE -7, total 42.5, kickoff weather not saved

script.base: Patriots lay 7 in a 42.5 game (implied NE 24.8, NYJ 17.8). Base flow is New England in front by about a score at half, Maye mixing Stevenson (33 carries / 133 yards over weeks 3-5) with Henderson if the ankle allows, then leaning run late. The Jets, as a 7-point dog, chase through Geno Smith; Garrett Wilson (28 targets, 238 yards in those three weeks) is the volume answer, with pressure from Dylan Parham being out and a 35% NE blitz pushing some of that into quick throws.
script.flip1: Shootout: both teams clear the low total, Maye stays in the 30-attempt range, and Doubs/Henry/Douglas plus Wilson/Williams all get full samples together. Correlated pass overs hit; the 42.5 under dies.
script.flip2: NE blowout (up 17+ by the second half): Stevenson/Henderson grind, Maye and NE pass-catcher snaps stall late, and Jets garbage-time throws pad Wilson or Isaiah Williams while NE skill overs die. The other kill-flip is an unsaved wind/rain slog that drags every yardage line under.

matchup.pressure: NE blitz rate 35%; Jets are worse when blitzed (EPA/db -0.06 vs +0.07 unblitzed), and Parham out should push that pressure home. NYJ blitz rate 39%; Maye is still positive vs blitz (EPA/db +0.07) but better when not blitzed (+0.21). Ossai out is the Jets' missing edge rusher, so Maye should have more time than the blitz rate alone implies.
matchup.bleeds: NE bleeds the middle (12.71 YPA) and explosives (14 passes of 20+ for 172 yards in 5 games); rush defense is the stronger side at 4.06 YPC and 10 runs of 10+. NYJ bleeds the run (4.41 YPC, 15 runs of 10+) and the middle (8.12 YPA), with 13 passes of 20+ for 177 yards.
matchup.overlap: Hunter Henry (11 targets, 111 yards, 68 air yards over weeks 3-5, about 6.2 air yards per target) is the clean overlap: a real TE into the Jets' middle bleed, with a 39% blitz that normally boosts TE catches. Isaiah Williams (16.9 air yards per target) is the personnel overlap, not the zone overlap: he attacks outside/deep, where NE's saved YPA is actually low, but the CBs who posted that split (Davis, Prunty) are out and NE has allowed 14 deep shots. Wilson into the 12.71 middle is the other primary-target overlap and was passed because 72.5 sits on his recent mean and Parham/blitz cuts the deep piece of his 9.1 aDOT.

The leader runs late, so Stevenson/Henderson carries rise if the game follows the spread; a 7-point spread is only a moderate blowout flag, so starter snap risk is real in the fourth but not a lock. Usage from shares, not raw averages: Wilson is 28 of 70 tracked Jets targets (40%); Henry is 11 of 84 tracked NE targets (13%); Williams is 7 of 70 (10%) but with Mitchell out that share is the sleeper, not the base share.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. New England led by two scores at half, Maye threw 19 times, and Henry's only look was a 5-yard checkdown while Stevenson and a limited Henderson ran the clock, repeating his 5-yard game. On the Jets side Williams never saw a target: Parham was out, New England blitzed, Geno lived in the quick game to Allen and Ruckert, Cooper was active, and the 16-to-73 yard sample was one explosive that did not travel. Belton played, a backup corner held the one deep shot, and the unsaved weather took the vertical game away. The counter-case is the low total plus a 2-target role, which is why both stays leans and the card is flagged rather than sized up.
slip_story: One story: dog-throws plus a Patriots offense that still has to move the ball through the middle, not a blowout clock-kill and not a game-total under. Henry over survives the base NE lead if there are about 28 Maye attempts; Williams over is the NYJ catch-up/shot piece of that same script. They can win together in a competitive Patriots win or the shootout flip. Do not add Stevenson or Allen rush overs (they need the opposite run script), do not add Wilson at 72.5 on the same Jets pass script without a number edge, and do not add TDs. Two legs, one market per player. Weather, final inactives, and a Henderson or Sadiq game-time scratch would force a rerun.
